verses.text: Ahithophel also said to Absalom, "Let me choose twelve thousand men and set out tonight to chase David.
I will attack him while he is tired and weak. I will make him panic, and all the people with him will run away. I will kill only the king,
and I will bring all the people back to you. When the man you are after is dead, everyone will come back, and all the people will be at peace."
This plan seemed good to Absalom and to all the leaders of Israel.
But Absalom said, "Call Hushai the Arkite too. Let's hear what he has to say."
When Hushai came, Absalom said to him, "Ahithophel has given this advice. Should we do what he says? If not, tell us your idea."
Hushai said to Absalom, "This time the advice Ahithophel has given is not good."

Hushai went on, "You know your father and his men. They are strong fighters, and they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have been stolen. Besides, your father is an experienced soldier. He will not spend the night with the people.

Even now he is probably hiding in a cave or some other place. If some of your men are killed at the start of the fighting, whoever hears about it will say, 'Absalom's followers are being slaughtered!'
Then even the bravest soldier, with a heart like a lion, will lose all courage. For all Israel knows that your father is a strong fighter and that the men with him are brave.
So this is my advice: Gather all Israel to you, from Dan to Beersheba, as many as the grains of sand by the sea. Then lead them into battle yourself.
We will attack David wherever he is found. We will come down on him like dew falling on the ground. Not one of them will be left alive, neither David nor any of his men.
If he goes into a city, all Israel will bring ropes to that city, and we will drag it down into the valley until not even a small stone is left there."

Absalom and all the men of Israel said, "The advice of Hushai the Arkite is better than the advice of Ahithophel." The LORD had decided to spoil Ahithophel's good advice, so that the LORD could bring disaster on Absalom.
Then Hushai told the priests Zadok and Abiathar, "Ahithophel advised Absalom and the leaders of Israel to do this, but I advised them to do that.

Now send a message to David quickly. Tell him, 'Do not spend the night at the river crossings in the wilderness. Cross over the river at once, or the king and all the people with him will be wiped out.'"
Jonathan and Ahimaaz were waiting at En Rogel. A servant girl would go and give them messages, and they would go and tell King David. They could not risk being seen going into the city.
But a young man saw them and told Absalom. So the two of them left quickly and went to the house of a man in Bahurim. He had a well in his yard, and they climbed down into it.
The man's wife took a cover and spread it over the opening of the well, and spread grain on top of it, so no one knew they were there.

When Absalom's servants came to the woman at the house, they asked, "Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?" The woman answered, "They have crossed over the stream." The men searched but could not find them, so they went back to Jerusalem.

After the men had gone, Ahimaaz and Jonathan climbed out of the well and went to tell King David. They said to him, "Get up and cross the river quickly, because Ahithophel has given advice against you."
So David and all the people with him got up and crossed the Jordan River. By sunrise, every one of them had crossed the Jordan.

When Ahithophel saw that his advice had not been followed, he put a saddle on his donkey and went home to his own town. He put his affairs in order and then hanged himself. He died and was buried in his father's tomb.
David came to Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with all the men of Israel.

Absalom had made Amasa commander of the army in place of Joab. Amasa was the son of a man named Ithra, an Israelite, who had married Abigail. She was the daughter of Nahash and the sister of Zeruiah, Joab's mother.
Israel and Absalom set up camp in the land of Gilead.
When David came to Mahanaim, Shobi son of Nahash from Rabbah of the Ammonites, Makir son of Ammiel from Lo Debar, and Barzillai from Rogelim in Gilead
brought beds, bowls, and clay pots. They also brought wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, and roasted seeds,
honey, butter, sheep, and cheese from cows' milk for David and the people with him to eat. They said, "The people must be hungry, tired, and thirsty in the wilderness."
